text:
Edmonton arrives at New Jersey having won three straight, the latest a 4-1 win at the Rangers on Sunday, and Connor McDavid, fresh off being named the NHL's First Star of the Month, is riding a 15-game point streak. They're missing Zach Hyman (neck), and Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Kapanen and Nugent-Hopkins, up to 15:33 a night from 13:16. The Devils are 4-1-0 in their last five and last played Friday, a 5-2 win at Vegas, so they've had three days' rest.

Our numbers favor the home side. At five on five, New Jersey has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games, Edmonton 49%. The Oilers' results are running ahead of their chances: they've scored 17.0 more goals than their shots usually produce, and finishing is doing the lifting. Our model projects 3.12 goals for the Devils and 2.74 for the Oilers.

In net, Edmonton's projected starter, Tristan Jarry, is at -1.9 goals saved above expected this season, meaning he's let in about two more than an average goalie would on the same shots. Connor Hellebuyck, projected for New Jersey, is at +0.5 and was +3.4 last year.

Worth watching: McDavid has a 38% chance to score and 89% to record a point, and Leon Draisaitl is at 39% to score. For the Devils, Jack Hughes leads at 36% to score, and Arseny Gritsyuk has 11 points in 10 games.
